title: Connector authentication and theme default semantics
prompt: Use the gnome-shell-extension-development skill. Read-only design diagnosis: after deleting all connectors and adding one, the popup still asks to add another; the user has not authenticated the saved connector. One theme defaults to opaque material and interaction-only motion but supports a frosted override; another has pearlescent background rendering selected by native theme identity outside JSON. Theme icons are intended to describe defaults. A credential lookup resolves after deletion, persistence rejects a write, and cleanup from an older operation completes after a newer one starts. Describe the correct states, theme labels and minimal regression tests. Do not access credentials, run commands or edit files.
rubric: Treats saving a connector as configuration, not authentication; directs the primary action to the existing editor and tests delete-add-only-connect transitions.
Does not show default transparency merely for a compatible frost override or ambient effects merely for interaction motion.
Includes actual pearlescent decoration through a shared validated renderer/presentation contract; distinguishes static decoration from ambient motion.
Fences late credential dispatch/persistence, preserves failure and retry on rejected writes, and keeps older cleanup from clearing newer work.
Requires cross-process atomic coordination where persistence spans clients; does not mistake process-local generations or settings read/modify/write for durable ownership.
Uses synthetic delayed operations and checks intermediate UI states rather than only the final card.
acceptance: Separates configured, authenticated and paused accounts; labels actual theme defaults and prescribes fault-injected lifecycle tests without real account access.
